subject: gk
question: Usually, the reduction in taxes will have a ______ multiplier effect compared to an increase in government spending on aggregate demand.
solution:
The correct answer is __**smaller.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Smaller -** When taxes are reduced, people have more disposable income to spend which leads to an increase in consumption and hence, an increase in aggregate demand. However, the multiplier effect of this increase in demand is smaller than the multiplier effect of an increase in government spending because some of the tax savings may be saved or used to pay off debt rather than spent immediately.
 
• **Higher **- An increase in government spending directly increases aggregate demand as it leads to an increase in government purchases, which in turn leads to an increase in the income of the suppliers. This increase in income leads to an increase in consumption, which again leads to an increase in demand. Thus, the multiplier effect of government spending is higher than the multiplier effect of tax reduction.
 
• **Equivalent** The multiplier effect of tax reduction is smaller than the multiplier effect of government spending.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The multiplier effect refers to the increase in national income that results from an increase in government spending or a reduction in taxes. It is the ratio of the change in national income to the change in government spending or taxes.
 
• Tax reduction leads to an increase in disposable income, which leads to an increase in consumption. However, some of the tax savings may not be spent immediately, which reduces the multiplier effect.
 
• Government spending leads to an increase in demand and income, which leads to an increase in consumption and a further increase in demand. This results in a higher multiplier effect.
 
• The equivalent option is incorrect because tax reduction has a smaller multiplier effect than government spending.
